---
title: "The business reports"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(contoso)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

contoso includes 1,127 fictional internal business reports about Contoso's
trading from May 2016 to the end of 2025. They are the documents a finance
team reads alongside its
sales data: weekly flashes, monthly reviews, quarterly country reports,
committee minutes and plan memos. Each is written by a named person in a
named business unit, published on a realistic date, and based on the
"mega" dataset from `create_contoso_duckdb("mega")`.

```{r}
#| label: read-reports
reports <- read_reports()
```

## Types of report

| Business area | Report type | Authors (in post on the publication date) | How often | A full year | 2016-2025 | Typical length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | `sales_flash`: Weekly Sales Flash | Sales Operations: Benjamin Castellanos to 2019, Priya Raman from 2020 | Weekly, every Monday | 52 (53 in 2020) | 501 | 430 words |
| Sales | `regional`: Quarterly Business Review | Country managers for the US, Germany, UK and Canada | Quarterly | 16 | 152 | 720 words |
| E-commerce and marketing | `ecommerce`: E-commerce Performance Review | Digital Commerce: Inès Duarte to 2021, Marcus Lindqvist from 2022 | Monthly | 12 | 115 | 640 words |
| Supply chain | `supply_chain`: Vendor & Supply Review | Supply Chain & Procurement: Victor Adeyemi to September 2020, Hannah Okafor from October 2020 | Monthly | 12 | 115 | 680 words |
| Manufacturing | `manufacturing`: Contoso, Ltd Plant Report | Tomasz Wisniewski, private-label plant | Monthly | 12 | 115 | 580 words |
| Pricing | `pricing`: Pricing & Promotions Committee Minutes | Chair: Robert Ashdown to 2022, Olivia Grant from 2023 | 5 meetings a year | 5 | 48 | 690 words |
| Planning and finance | `aop`: Annual Operating Plan memo | Corporate Planning: Margaret Holloway to June 2020, Daniel Okoye from July 2020 | Once, before each year from 2017 | 1 | 9 | 1,040 words |
| Operations | `alert`: Supply alerts and operations notices | Supply Chain, Retail Operations | When something happens | 2-5 | 34 | 310 words |
| External market | `industry`: Sector Review | Northbridge Retail Insights, an outside analyst | Quarterly | 4 | 38 | 690 words |

2016 is a partial year, because the data starts on 18 May 2016: weekly
flashes run from week 21, monthly reports from June, quarterly reports
cover Q3 and Q4 only, and there is no plan or budget.

```{r}
#| label: count-by-type
reports |>
  dplyr::count(report_type, unit, sort = TRUE)
```

Each type follows its own template:

| Report type | Sections |
|---|---|
| `sales_flash` | Headline, key numbers table, Channel, Country, Category, Watch list |
| `regional` | Executive summary, Performance vs last year and budget, Category highlights, Store operations, Customers and competitors, Priorities next quarter, Asks of HQ |
| `ecommerce` | Headline, Channel mix, Online performance vs last year and budget, Online category performance, Site and marketing notes, Priorities for next month |
| `supply_chain` | Summary, Vendor scorecard (red/amber/green by manufacturer), Issues and mitigations, Outlook |
| `manufacturing` | Summary, Sell-through by category and product line, Cost and yield, Capacity and launches, Risks |
| `pricing` | Attendees, Review of recent performance, Discussion, Decisions, Action items |
| `aop` | Summary of targets, Key assumptions, Phasing through the year, Risks to the plan, Accountabilities by unit |
| `alert` | What happened, Impact, Actions, Next update |
| `industry` | Key takeaways, Demand by category, Channels, Pricing and promotions, Outlook |

## A sample report

The Weekly Sales Flash for week 20, in full:

```{r}
#| label: sample-report
sample <- dplyr::filter(reports, id == "sales-flash-2025-w20")
cat(sample$body)
```

## Dimensions of a report

### Metadata

Every report carries the same eight metadata fields, plus its text:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | `sales-flash-2025-w20` |
| `title` | text | `r sample$title` |
| `unit` | text | `r sample$unit` |
| `author` | text | `r sample$author` |
| `report_type` | text | `r sample$report_type` |
| `period_start` | date | `r sample$period_start` |
| `period_end` | date | `r sample$period_end` |
| `published` | date | `r sample$published` |
| `body` | Markdown text | the report itself |

`period_start` and `period_end` give the period a report covers, and
`published` gives the date it was released. The gap between them varies by
type: a weekly flash comes out the day after its week ends, a regional
review about 12 days after its quarter. The plan memo is negative: each one
is published in December of the year before the one it covers.



### Business dimensions

The figures in each report are cut by the same dimensions as the contoso
data. Which cuts a report uses depends on its type:

| Report type | Period | Breakdowns | Compared with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sales_flash` | Week | Total, channel (online / stores), country, category | Prior week, same week last year |
| `regional` | Quarter | One country: total and category | Prior quarter, last year, budget |
| `ecommerce` | Month | Channel mix, online total, online by category | Prior month, last year, budget |
| `supply_chain` | Month | Total, manufacturer, category | Prior month, last year, budget |
| `manufacturing` | Month | Contoso, Ltd products: total, category, product line | Prior month, last year |
| `pricing` | The 8 weeks before the meeting | Total, category, channel | Prior 8 weeks, last year |
| `aop` | Full year, 2017-2025 | Budget by channel, country, category and month | The previous year's actuals |
| `alert` | One event | Vendors, categories and regions affected | None |
| `industry` | Quarter | Market-level demand by category and channel (no Contoso figures) | Market last year |

The values those breakdowns take:

| Dimension | Values |
|---|---|
| Channel | Online, Stores |
| Country | United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Australia, plus Online |
| Category | Computers, Cell phones, Home Appliances, TV and Video, Cameras and camcorders, Audio, Games and Toys, Music, Movies and Audio Books |
| Manufacturer | 11, including Contoso, Ltd, the company's own private label |

### Measures

The numbers quoted in the reports are these measures:

| Measure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Net revenue | Sales after discounts, in USD |
| Change vs prior period | Against the previous week, month or quarter |
| Change vs last year | Against the same period a year earlier |
| Variance to budget | Against that year's Annual Operating Plan (from 2017) |
| Gross margin % | Gross margin as a share of net revenue |
| Discount % | Discounts as a share of gross revenue |
| Cost ratio | Cost of goods as a share of gross revenue |
| Units | Units sold |

## The years in the reports

Reports run from the first weekly flash in May 2016 to the last reviews of
2025, published in January 2026:

```{r}
#| label: reports-by-year
reports |>
  dplyr::count(year = format(published, "%Y"), name = "reports")
```

Together they tell one continuous story, and every event explains a
movement in the data:

| Year | What happens |
|---|---|
| 2016 | A new sales system goes live on 18 May, which is why the data starts then |
| 2017 | A laptop and smartphone boom and the last big wave of new customers; smartphones replace compact cameras |
| 2018 | A price-list reset, four store openings and a one-off anniversary sale |
| 2019 | The best year so far, driven by a new loyalty programme that makes existing customers buy more often |
| 2020 | A rush to redeem loyalty points, then a component shortage that cuts stock across the range |
| 2021 | The shortage at its worst, then recovery |
| 2022 | Marketplaces, a TV and air-conditioning boom and a strong dollar |
| 2023 | A record year |
| 2024 | A difficult year, as customers buy less often and the best ones start to leave |
| 2025 | A marketplace exit, a TV range reset, a store refit programme ("Store Next"), a product safety notice and a PC refresh |

The stocktake, summer shutdown and holiday season recur every year. Each
author only knows what their unit would know on the publication date, and
people change roles over the years.

### Glossary of terms

The terms the reports use, and the phrasings to search for, are defined in
a glossary:

```{r}
#| label: glossary

fp <- system.file("extdata", "reports", "glossary.yaml", package = "contoso")
glossary <- yaml12::read_yaml(fp)
glossary$win_back$definition
```

Some reports are deliberately wrong. A few authors misread the data or
credit the wrong cause, as real business writing does. The package does not
say which, so an FP&A assistant has to find them by checking the reports
against the data.
